title: Allow injection of Spring-managed beans into Hazelcast components

timeline.message:
Inject SpringManagedContext into Hazelcast configuration

Fixes gh-19487
When Spring Boot creates Hazelcast configuration and the Hazelcast-Spring
integration module is available on a classpath then use SpringManagedContext.

This makes it possible to inject Spring managed beans into objects
instantiated by Hazelcast.
timeline.author: Jaromir Hamala

timeline.body:
Fixes #19487

When Spring Boot creates Hazelcast configuration and the Hazelcast-Spring
integration module is available on a classpath then inject SpringManagedContext
into Hazelcast configuration. 

This change makes it possible to inject Spring managed beans into objects
instantiated by Hazelcast. 

I'm not too familiar with Spring Boot so chances are the code is not idiomatic. It looks rather complex for what is basically an if-else condition. Any guidance is very much appreciated.
the same change should be probably done in the client auto-configuration.

I'm not sure if this is the right way to introduce a fallback. 

It appears it's dependant on the ordering of methods in a class. If I move this method above `springManagedContextConfigurationCustomizer()` then both beans are constructed. So I reckon there is a less fragile way, any hint is appreciated.

reply.body: I guess the trick is to use a separate configuration class, take a look: https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/blob/main/spring-boot-project/spring-boot-autoconfigure/src/main/java/org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/jdbc/DataSourceAutoConfiguration.java#L66-L72

Thanks for this suggestion, I was considering it, but it looked like an overkill to me. Too much ceremony, for my taste anyway. 

Given the other changes `EMPTY_CUSTOMIZER` is not needed anymore the ordering of bean factory methods is not a concern anymore.

timeline.body: Couldn't we use `List<ConfigurationCustomizer> customizers` to avoid the need of `EMPTY_CUSTOMIZER` and at the same time support multiple customizers?

reply.body: This is a good suggestion, thank you. I'm not sure at this point that we need to support multiple beans, but avoiding the need for `EMPTY_CUSTOMIZER` is a good goal. Our style is the achieve that via Spring Framework's `ObjectProvider` and its `getIfAvailable()` method.

Good suggestions, thanks to both of you! 

I pushed an update with ObjectProvider and indeed it simplified the code quite a bit. 

I also made the customizer to return `void`. It makes it less flexible, but that's not a concern here. It led to further code simplification and it's also aligned with most of the other customizers I saw in the Spring codebase.

timeline.body: Why `private`? We don't want to expose customizers functionality to users or it's just the first phase?

reply.body: Until we have a concrete need for other customisers, I'd prefer to minimise the surface area of the public API.

timeline.message:
Mark ConfigurationCustomizer as a FunctionInterface

Co-authored-by: Łukasz Dziedziul <l.dziedziul@gmail.com>
timeline.author: Jaromir Hamala

timeline.message:
Make the Customizer optional

This eliminates the need for EMPTY_CUSTOMIZER.
timeline.author: Jaromir Hamala
